title: CDIAC Meeting - Summary of Discussions Among Members of the Community Depository Institutions Advisory Council
summary: The Community Depository Institutions Advisory Council met on April 11, 2024, and reported that the economy remains surprisingly resilient despite persistent inflationary pressures driven by strong consumer demand, though a bifurcation exists between upper- and lower-income groups. Council members noted that inflation has moderated from its peak but remains stubbornly high, with services inflation persisting due to labor costs while goods inflation is slowing. The Council expressed doubts about achieving the 2% inflation target in the near term.
key_points: Economy remains resilient despite inflationary challenges, with persistent bifurcation between upper- and lower-income households
Inflation has moderated from peak but remains stubbornly high, driven by strong consumer demand and labor costs
Goods inflation is slowing while services inflation persists due to associated labor costs
Labor markets remain tight for non-skilled and blue-collar workers; pay increases moderating from 6-7% to 4-5%
Housing prices remain restrictive for most consumers despite moderation; affordability varies regionally
Technology costs rising significantly with year-over-year increases of up to 10% in 2024 versus prior 2-3% average
Council members expressed doubts about near-term feasibility of the 2% inflation target
why_it_matters: This CDIAC meeting summary provides a real-time snapshot of economic conditions from regional depository institution perspectives, capturing ground-level observations on inflation persistence, labor market tightness, and housing affordability challenges that inform Federal Reserve policy deliberations.
macro_context: Regional Fed Council feedback indicates inflation remains above target with services component particularly sticky due to labor costs. Labor markets are loosening gradually as wage growth moderates from 6-7% to 4-5%. Housing affordability remains a constraint. The Council's skepticism about near-term 2% target achievement suggests prolonged restrictive policy expectations.
